basis: Meningioma arising within the cerebral ventricles.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis.
Carcinoma of frontal sinus mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Beta-globin disorder causing red-cell abnormalities, usually mild microcytic anaemia.
Focal epilepsy originating in the primary motor cortex.
Cerebellar degeneration, developmental delay and intellectual disability; abnormal saccades and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Inherited palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with blistering and ulceration; associated tinea is a separate infection.
Congenital acetabular dysplasia and hip dislocation define a skeletal and joint disorder.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy; scoliosis in 3/6 (~50%) supports skeletal involvement. Nystagmus is neurologic; visual impairment and stones each occur in 1/6.
KMT2E-related neurodevelopmental syndrome with global developmental and speech delay; no other axis has established common direct damage.
Craniosynostosis, pulmonary valve stenosis and ventriculomegaly/intellectual disability define the syndrome; ectopic anus is another defining malformation, retained as the fourth axis.
Delayed endocrine maturation with transient hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; delayed bone age does not establish skeletal damage.
Thymic gland tumour classified under endocrine gland neoplasm; associated autoimmune disease is separate, and epithelial thymic tumours are not blood-cell neoplasms.
Parainfluenza type 2 causes respiratory tract infection, commonly involving upper airways and the larynx.
Aniridia, intellectual disability and obesity define WAGRO; proteinuria in 1/2 supports renal damage beyond tumour risk. Skeletal, dental and vascular findings omitted at cap.
MYH7-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects cardiac muscle; the gene alone does not establish skeletal myopathy.
Familial dilated cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ventricular function in 3/3 patients.
Callosal agenesis, cataracts and immunodeficiency define Vici; cardiomyopathy occurs in 80-99%. Renal anomalies/RTA and myopathy (~33%) omitted at cap; skin hypopigmentation is non-damaging.
Benign tumour of connective and soft tissues; musculoskeletal ancestry supports this axis across the umbrella.
Astrocytic tumour arising in the brainstem.
Squamous cell carcinoma originating in skin.
Combined bladder and prostate inflammation; bladder belongs to renal, prostate has no axis. Infection or autoimmune causation is not established by this concept.
Congenital complete atresia of the mitral valve.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in the bronchus or lung.
Testicular trophoblastic germ-cell tumour; reproductive origin does not establish endocrine-gland disease.
